correctness.rationale: The row/column domination and bipartite incidence connectivity equivalences are direct. Minimality forces exactly one complete bipartition, acyclicity and leaf vertices only on that complete side. Deletion of each allowed edge destroys connectivity or coverage, proving sufficiency. Surjective bipartite Prüfer words give the exact multiplicity. A direct independent graph-definition subset test verifies the structural characterization and full polynomial for seven small boards; these are checks rather than proofs of the infinite result.

originality.rationale: The full inspected Mertens rook domination article gives ordinary domination polynomial and minimum values, not the minimal connected subfamily; the general ESA 2022 enumerating-minimal-connected-dominators paper gives algorithms and extremal complexity, not the rook board structural tree classification. Semantic searches of published mathematical records and the accessible existing local ledger found no equivalent or stronger result. The exact one-sided-leaf bipartite-tree census, Stirling-number formula and gapped cardinality spectra do not follow from cited scalar/ordinary results without the new minimal-connected characterization. Priority remains subject to unindexed earlier work.
residual_risks: An unindexed paper or an article phrased entirely in connected edge domination/line-graph terms could contain equivalent coverage without surfacing in searches.
A generic computer algebra database could supply small numerical coefficients; it does not by itself certify symbolic uniqueness or novelty.

value.rationale: An exact all-size irredundant connected-domination census for a natural product-graph family is a substantive refinement of ordinary domination. The tree bijection yields nontrivial Stirling-number coefficients and a provable unbounded gap in the sizes of inclusion-minimal connected dominating sets on thin rectangles. Those structural phenomena are not implied by the known scalar domination parameter.
